video_title: Solana's Historic Governance Vote — While Robinhood Invades Its Meme Coin Turf
gist: Nick Almond, head of governance at the JTO Foundation, walks through Solana's first enshrined onchain governance round (SGP1 constitution ratified, SGP2 double-disinflation passed by ~8 seconds, SGP3 compute-unit fee pricing rejected) and how JTO's liquid staking token swung ~10M SOL via a 10%-TVL quorum trigger. He argues Solana's 87% network-revenue decline is partly self-inflicted margin compression from trebling block size, frames Robin Hood chain's memecoin/tokenized-stock surge as a fast-follow arms race rather than a structural threat, and expects a fundamentals-then-hype repricing over the next 12-18 months with value accrual via buyback-and-burn token models.

insights.claim: Solana has replaced its ad-hoc off-chain voting (which minted proposal-specific, memecoin-like tokens that validators sent back to tally accounts) with an enshrined onchain governance primitive, first exercised in the SGP1/SGP2/SGP3 round.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Solana now has a repeatable, auditable mechanism to change monetary policy and fee markets, so SOL holders must price protocol economics as a live governance variable rather than a fixed schedule.
insights.quote: we've uh effectively built an enshrined onchain governance primitive and that's what's just launched effectively

insights.claim: The new 'voter override' mechanism lets any Solana stake account vote against its own validator's choice, shifting validators from controllers of the network to stewards and pushing voting power down to individual SOL stakers.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Large validators can no longer be treated as reliable proxies for vote outcomes, so forecasting Solana policy changes now requires modeling retail and LST staker behavior.
insights.quote: which effectively allows any stake account on the network to override their validator

insights.claim: Solana's proposal path is permissionless in practice: anyone who can convince a validator holding over 100k stake can submit a network-level proposal, and 15% validator support forces a full network vote.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: A low submission bar means a steady stream of economically consequential proposals on SOL inflation, fees and burn, each a potential catalyst or overhang.
insights.quote: anyone who can convince a validator with over 100k stake can put a proposal up at the network level. um and if they can convince 15% of the validators it's worth voting on, the whole network votes on it

insights.claim: Solana proposals become immutable once triggered, and participants generally only read them once voting opens, which turned SGP3 into a last-minute controversy rather than a negotiated change.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Expect volatile, late-breaking vote outcomes on Solana until the constitution is amended, which makes governance headlines a short-term risk factor for SOL and for apps with fee exposure.
insights.quote: people don't really read these proposals until you're voting

insights.claim: Solana's passed double-disinflation proposal halves the time to terminal issuance: SOL now reaches 1.5% tail inflation in roughly 3 years instead of about 9.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: SOL staking yield compresses far faster than previously scheduled, cutting dilution for holders while shrinking the carry that yield-driven staking demand depends on.
insights.quote: in now 3 years time uh the network will get to one and a half% inflation and we'll stay there indefinitely

insights.claim: The disinflation vote was contested because large staking providers earn a slice of pass-through inflation rewards, so accelerating disinflation directly compresses their revenue.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Custodial and exchange staking businesses on Solana face a structural margin squeeze, a direct read-through for firms monetizing SOL staking spreads.
insights.quote: So we're asking them to earn less money by being staking providers.

insights.claim: The Solana disinflation vote was failing until roughly 8 seconds before it closed and was decided with 22 slots remaining, with Kraken's late switch identified as the deciding swing.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Outcomes of Solana economic votes can hinge on a single exchange-scale voter in the final seconds, so positioning ahead of a governance result carries binary risk.
insights.quote: the vote was decided uh with 22 slots um remaining which is about 8 seconds

insights.claim: Smaller long-tail Solana validators, who had opposed earlier inflation cuts because they depend more on block rewards, swung in favor this time under the influence of Mert campaigning for SOL as a long-term investable asset.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: The validator base is becoming persuadable by long-horizon asset arguments, raising the odds that future proposals to cut issuance or raise burn also pass.

insights.claim: The earlier SIMD28 inflation proposal failed even though Toly, Multicoin and other influential backers supported it, which the guest treats as hard evidence that Solana's stake is not captured by insiders.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Investors underwriting Solana on a 'controlled by insiders' thesis have a concrete counterexample where a multi-billion-dollar economic vote went against the core backers.
insights.quote: this is a, you know, 3040 billion dollar vote that's happening using the network stake on the network

insights.claim: The guest frames the disinflation vote as the network explicitly choosing long-term asset quality over short-term staking income, trading validator revenue today for lower dilution later.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Signals a policy regime where Solana keeps tightening issuance, supporting a monetary-premium thesis for SOL but weakening yield-based valuation models.
insights.quote: almost forego short-term reward for long-term gain

insights.claim: JTO built a 'quorum trigger' under JIP30 so that if at least 10% of JitoSOL TVL votes in a pre-vote signaling round, the entire stake pool votes as one bloc; 13% participated and roughly 10 million SOL was cast in the disinflation vote.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: A minority of an LST's holders can now move a swing bloc in Solana monetary policy, making LST governance design a real variable in predicting vote outcomes.

insights.claim: The quorum-trigger design gives an LST holder up to 10x leverage on their voting power relative to their stake, positioning governance utility as a differentiator in a market with roughly 2,000 Solana liquid staking tokens.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Governance uplift could become a competitive moat for LSTs in a crowded field, a factor to watch for LST market-share shifts and token demand.
insights.quote: if you're a GSO soul holder, you get potentially up to 10x the voting power

insights.claim: JitoSOL's stake pool dynamically delegates across roughly 350 validators, and JTO used the new voter override to recall that delegated voting power from validators and vote it according to LST holders' preference.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Delegated stake in pools is no longer validator-controlled voting power, which changes how to count voting blocs when forecasting Solana proposals.

insights.claim: The guest argues decentralization should be scored across separate technical, economic and political dimensions rather than as a single fundamentalist standard, and blames early DAO failures on the all-or-nothing version.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Gives a structured way to compare L1s on decentralization risk instead of relying on validator counts, useful when institutions diligence chain selection.

insights.claim: Solana's IBRL push forces validators to the absolute frontier of data-center hardware, and the validator set has already compressed from about 1,000 to around 700 with further compression expected.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Falling validator counts are an accepted cost of Solana's latency strategy, a concrete metric to track against the chain's institutional and censorship-resistance pitch.
insights.quote: we're talking 700 or so validators has compressed a bit down from a thousand

insights.claim: The guest claims his own analysis shows Ethereum and Solana stake sits in almost exactly the same data centers with nearly identical geographic distribution, so Ethereum's decentralization edge is mainly its 32-ETH solo validators acting as catastrophe insurance.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: If institutions verify this, Ethereum's core differentiation pitch for tokenized assets weakens and chain choice shifts toward execution quality and distribution.
insights.quote: The majority of stake um on the Ethereum network lives in almost exactly the same uh data centers as uh as the Salana stake.

insights.claim: The arrival of permissioned-validator-set networks such as Tempo and Canton, some with an entire validator set in one data center, resets the centralization baseline and makes Solana look competitive by comparison.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Institutional chains competing for the same tokenized-asset flow are far more centralized, so decentralization may stop being the deciding purchase criterion.

themes.theme: Revenue decline vs deliberate margin compression

insights.claim: Solana's first-half network revenue is down 87% year over year per 21Shares, and memecoin share of trading fell from 40% to 16%.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: The headline fee collapse is the bear case on SOL and the baseline any recovery thesis has to beat.

insights.claim: Part of Solana's network revenue decline is self-inflicted: the network trebled block size, which reduced competition for blockspace and therefore lowered priority fees and JTO tips, as a deliberate choice to absorb 10x-50x future demand.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Fee-based valuation of SOL can misread engineered capacity expansion as demand loss; watch throughput and app revenue rather than network fees alone.
insights.quote: part of the reason why that network rev has dropped is because we've um trebled the size of the blocks

insights.claim: Solana launched about 1.7 million tokens in a single week, an all-time high by a considerable margin, even while memecoin fee share collapsed.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Token issuance activity and fee capture have decoupled, so issuance counts are a poor proxy for monetizable demand on Solana.
insights.quote: I think we launched 1.7 million coins this week or something like that which was a all-time high for the network by a considerable margin

insights.claim: The guest argues the metrics that matter this cycle are real-world-asset TVL and tokenized equity volume rather than network revenue or memecoin share.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Reorients the SOL scorecard toward RWA and tokenized-stock throughput, where the host notes Robin Hood chain and Binance currently lead and Solana ranks only top three to five.

insights.claim: Robin Hood, which the guest says has roughly 10 million exchange users to funnel onto its adjacent chain, built its own chain rather than deploying on Solana purely to own the rails and capture rents through a single sequencer, accepting fees that are currently higher than Ethereum mainnet.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Any large distribution-owning fintech will likely choose its own L2 for rent capture over an L1, capping the share of tokenized-equity flow general-purpose L1s can win.
insights.quote: Robin Hood's fees are higher than mainet recently

insights.claim: The memecoin-paired-with-tokenized-stock product that took off on Robin Hood chain was quickly replicated on Solana via stonks.fun, where users are airdropped Nvidia stock and pair it with novel memecoins, and the guest dismisses it as a fast-follow arms race with little durable edge.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Product-level moats in the memecoin trenches are near zero, so the trade is on distribution and user base rather than first-mover novelty.
insights.quote: As soon as someone launches it, someone's going to launch something something comparable.

insights.claim: The guest positions Solana as a generalized L1 with more shots on goal than app-specific competitors, citing an incubator pipeline via Superteams, prediction markets, expected NFT and social revivals, and new agentic payment channels claimed to handle around a million transactions per second.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: The bull case for SOL rests on optionality across unknown future metas rather than defending memecoin or perp share, so watch new app categories over current fee league tables.
insights.quote: if something's going to happen in crypto, it's likely going to happen on Salana just because we're playing the entire field

insights.claim: The guest says buying large partnerships is not Solana's main strategy; organic growth plus existing network effects is the pitch to builders who lack their own exchange-scale user funnel.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Do not expect a headline Robin Hood-style partnership catalyst for SOL; growth should show up as a broadening app base instead.

themes.theme: SOL value accrual and next cycle

insights.claim: The rejected SGP3 fee proposal, which would have priced transactions by compute units and raised the SOL cost of running major apps like Phoenix by an estimated 10x to 100x, is back in the proposal track and likely to return as a sequence of smaller changes.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: A compute-unit fee regime remains a live risk to the cost base of high-throughput Solana apps and a potential future source of SOL burn.
insights.quote: the number of soul that they would have needed to run their app I think maybe 10 or even 100xed

insights.claim: JTO will route five or six revenue lines into its DAO next year and connect all of them directly to the token through buybacks and burns, which the guest says reflects a network-wide phase change toward tight coupling of app revenue and token value.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Crypto tokens are converging on cash-flow-linked models, which makes revenue-per-token screens a usable valuation tool for Solana app tokens.
insights.quote: we've got five or six revenue lines that come into the Dow next year all of that is getting connected directly to the token in the form of buyback and burns

insights.claim: The guest dismisses the intensity of inflation and burn debates as bear-market thinking that fades once prices reprice on the next hype wave.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Suggests tokenomics tightening is a sentiment-driven theme; its perceived importance may be a contrarian indicator of where the cycle stands.
insights.quote: I find a lot of the inflation conversations to be a kind of bare market thinking

insights.claim: The guest predicts another crypto hype wave within roughly 12 to 18 months, driven by off-chain institutional capital moving onchain and fought over mainly by Ethereum and Solana, with price appreciation itself triggering the hype in a chicken-and-egg loop.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Frames a 12-18 month horizon for a flows-driven repricing concentrated in ETH and SOL rather than broad altcoin beta.

insights.claim: Real-time onchain revenue visibility, where a project's revenue lines can be read block by block, will let traditional analysts build discounted-cash-flow style theses instead of waiting on quarterly earnings.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: Crypto assets with transparent onchain revenue may earn a re-rating as traditional analysts adopt them, favoring protocols that publish clean revenue data.
insights.quote: you can see the revenue lines block by block

insights.claim: JTO's consumer trading front end JTX, live only two to three months, already generates more fees on some days than all of the firm's other product lines combined, and about half the team still works on block-building infrastructure aimed at deterministic institutional execution.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: The consumer interface layer is monetizing faster than core MEV and block-building infrastructure, a template for infrastructure projects moving up the stack toward end users.
insights.quote: JTX is already on some days generating more fees than all of our other uh product lines put together

insights.claim: The guest rejects the growing institutional belief that compliant finance cannot run on permissionless blockchains and says execution quality on Solana can eventually match or beat traditional best execution.
insights.speaker: Nick Almond
insights.so_what: If permissionless chains can deliver deterministic, compliant execution, the case for permissioned institutional chains like Tempo and Canton weakens.
